values: A binding agreement between parties: signed contracts, statements of work, NDAs, terms of service, amendments. Choose this when the document sets out obligations the parties have agreed to, not when it only proposes them.

A request for payment or a record of one: invoices, receipts, credit notes, payment confirmations, account statements. Choose this when the document names amounts owed or paid, not when it merely discusses pricing.
Instructions for work to be done: project briefs, requirements, technical specifications, design briefs, acceptance criteria. Choose this when the document tells someone what to build or deliver.
A finding presented to a reader: research reports, analyses, audits, post-mortems, reviews of work already done. Choose this when the document draws conclusions from evidence.
A record of what was said and decided: minutes, call notes, interview transcripts, workshop write-ups. Choose this when the document records a discussion rather than making an argument of its own.

Text written to be published to an audience: landing-page copy, social posts, ads, newsletters, press releases, product descriptions. Choose this when the intended readers are customers rather than colleagues.
Structured records rather than prose: spreadsheets, CSV exports, query results, logs, metric dumps. Choose this when the substance is rows and columns, even if prose introduces them.
Something kept to be consulted later: documentation, guides, handbooks, policies, style guides, glossaries, FAQs. Choose this when the document is written to be returned to rather than read once.
An offer put to someone for a decision: proposals, quotes, estimates, pitches, tenders, bids. Choose this when the document asks the reader to accept, buy or approve something.
Slides made to be presented: decks, pitch decks, keynotes, workshop slides, training slides. Choose this when the document is structured as a sequence of slides.
What will happen and when: project plans, roadmaps, timelines, schedules, OKRs, checklists. Choose this when the document sets out future work rather than recording past work.
A message between people: emails, letters, chat exports, memos, announcements. Choose this when the document is addressed to a reader rather than written for the record.
A document meant to be filled in or copied: templates, forms, checklists to complete, questionnaires, boilerplate. Choose this when the substance is blanks to be completed.
Money: budgets, pricing, costs, revenue, payments, forecasts, financial reporting.
Legal exposure: contracts, compliance, licensing, liability, regulation, privacy law.
Building software: architecture, code, APIs, infrastructure, deployment, defects.
How something looks or is used: visual design, user experience, wireframes, brand assets, typography.
Reaching an audience: campaigns, channels, positioning, messaging, growth, brand.
Winning customers: pipeline, proposals, negotiations, customer calls, quotas, renewals.
What to build and why: roadmaps, feature decisions, user research, prioritisation, release scope.
Running the business day to day: process, vendors, logistics, internal tooling, procurement.
The people in the organisation: hiring, onboarding, performance, roles, staff policies.
Where the organisation is going: plans, market analysis, competitive positioning, long-range goals.
Protecting systems and data: access control, vulnerabilities, incidents, audits, threat models.
Gathering evidence before deciding: market research, interviews, literature reviews, experiments.
Helping existing customers: tickets, complaints, help-desk answers, escalations, satisfaction, troubleshooting.
Measuring and analysing: metrics, dashboards, SQL, experiments, tracking, statistics, reporting on numbers.
Working with other organisations: partners, integrations, resellers, agencies, joint ventures, sponsorship.
Raising and reporting to funders: fundraising, cap tables, investor updates, grants, valuation.
Meeting rules: audits, certifications, GDPR, policies, regulatory filings, risk registers.
Models and agents: LLMs, prompts, training data, evaluation, AI agents, automation with AI.
Making things to publish: articles, blog posts, video, copywriting, editorial calendars, social media.
People around the product: users, forums, Discord, ambassadors, feedback, events for members.
Explaining how things work: guides, manuals, READMEs, runbooks, API references, onboarding docs.
Gatherings: conferences, meetups, webinars, workshops, trade shows, travel and logistics.
Teaching and learning: courses, tutorials, curricula, coaching, certification, learning material.
Distributed ledgers: Cardano, wallets, tokens, smart contracts, NFTs, staking, on-chain payments.
Find, reproduce, or fix a defect where existing behavior differs from the expected result.
Respond to a service disruption, assess its impact, restore service, or document the incident.
Test a hypothesis with a trial or comparison and use the result to decide what to try next.
Choose between alternatives and record the trade-offs behind the choice.
Transfer ownership of work with the context and next steps the recipient needs.

A record of what was said and decided: minutes, call notes, interview transcripts, workshop write-ups. Choose this when the document records a discussion rather than making an argument of its own.

Text written to be published to an audience: landing-page copy, social posts, ads, newsletters, press releases, product descriptions. Choose this when the intended readers are customers rather than colleagues.
Structured records rather than prose: spreadsheets, CSV exports, query results, logs, metric dumps. Choose this when the substance is rows and columns, even if prose introduces them.
Something kept to be consulted later: documentation, guides, handbooks, policies, style guides, glossaries, FAQs. Choose this when the document is written to be returned to rather than read once.
An offer put to someone for a decision: proposals, quotes, estimates, pitches, tenders, bids. Choose this when the document asks the reader to accept, buy or approve something.
Slides made to be presented: decks, pitch decks, keynotes, workshop slides, training slides. Choose this when the document is structured as a sequence of slides.
What will happen and when: project plans, roadmaps, timelines, schedules, OKRs, checklists. Choose this when the document sets out future work rather than recording past work.
A message between people: emails, letters, chat exports, memos, announcements. Choose this when the document is addressed to a reader rather than written for the record.
A document meant to be filled in or copied: templates, forms, checklists to complete, questionnaires, boilerplate. Choose this when the substance is blanks to be completed.
Money: budgets, pricing, costs, revenue, payments, forecasts, financial reporting.
Legal exposure: contracts, compliance, licensing, liability, regulation, privacy law.
Building software: architecture, code, APIs, infrastructure, deployment, defects.
How something looks or is used: visual design, user experience, wireframes, brand assets, typography.
Reaching an audience: campaigns, channels, positioning, messaging, growth, brand.
Winning customers: pipeline, proposals, negotiations, customer calls, quotas, renewals.
What to build and why: roadmaps, feature decisions, user research, prioritisation, release scope.
Running the business day to day: process, vendors, logistics, internal tooling, procurement.
The people in the organisation: hiring, onboarding, performance, roles, staff policies.
Where the organisation is going: plans, market analysis, competitive positioning, long-range goals.
Protecting systems and data: access control, vulnerabilities, incidents, audits, threat models.
Gathering evidence before deciding: market research, interviews, literature reviews, experiments.
Helping existing customers: tickets, complaints, help-desk answers, escalations, satisfaction, troubleshooting.
Measuring and analysing: metrics, dashboards, SQL, experiments, tracking, statistics, reporting on numbers.
Working with other organisations: partners, integrations, resellers, agencies, joint ventures, sponsorship.
Raising and reporting to funders: fundraising, cap tables, investor updates, grants, valuation.
Meeting rules: audits, certifications, GDPR, policies, regulatory filings, risk registers.
Models and agents: LLMs, prompts, training data, evaluation, AI agents, automation with AI.
Making things to publish: articles, blog posts, video, copywriting, editorial calendars, social media.
People around the product: users, forums, Discord, ambassadors, feedback, events for members.
Explaining how things work: guides, manuals, READMEs, runbooks, API references, onboarding docs.
Gatherings: conferences, meetups, webinars, workshops, trade shows, travel and logistics.
Teaching and learning: courses, tutorials, curricula, coaching, certification, learning material.
Distributed ledgers: Cardano, wallets, tokens, smart contracts, NFTs, staking, on-chain payments.
Find, reproduce, or fix a defect where existing behavior differs from the expected result.
Respond to a service disruption, assess its impact, restore service, or document the incident.
Test a hypothesis with a trial or comparison and use the result to decide what to try next.
Choose between alternatives and record the trade-offs behind the choice.
Transfer ownership of work with the context and next steps the recipient needs.

values: A binding agreement between parties: signed contracts, statements of work, NDAs, terms of service, amendments. Choose this when the document sets out obligations the parties have agreed to, not when it only proposes them.

A request for payment or a record of one: invoices, receipts, credit notes, payment confirmations, account statements. Choose this when the document names amounts owed or paid, not when it merely discusses pricing.
Instructions for work to be done: project briefs, requirements, technical specifications, design briefs, acceptance criteria. Choose this when the document tells someone what to build or deliver.
A finding presented to a reader: research reports, analyses, audits, post-mortems, reviews of work already done. Choose this when the document draws conclusions from evidence.
A record of what was said and decided: minutes, call notes, interview transcripts, workshop write-ups. Choose this when the document records a discussion rather than making an argument of its own.

Text written to be published to an audience: landing-page copy, social posts, ads, newsletters, press releases, product descriptions. Choose this when the intended readers are customers rather than colleagues.
Structured records rather than prose: spreadsheets, CSV exports, query results, logs, metric dumps. Choose this when the substance is rows and columns, even if prose introduces them.
Something kept to be consulted later: documentation, guides, handbooks, policies, style guides, glossaries, FAQs. Choose this when the document is written to be returned to rather than read once.
An offer put to someone for a decision: proposals, quotes, estimates, pitches, tenders, bids. Choose this when the document asks the reader to accept, buy or approve something.
Slides made to be presented: decks, pitch decks, keynotes, workshop slides, training slides. Choose this when the document is structured as a sequence of slides.
What will happen and when: project plans, roadmaps, timelines, schedules, OKRs, checklists. Choose this when the document sets out future work rather than recording past work.
A message between people: emails, letters, chat exports, memos, announcements. Choose this when the document is addressed to a reader rather than written for the record.
A document meant to be filled in or copied: templates, forms, checklists to complete, questionnaires, boilerplate. Choose this when the substance is blanks to be completed.
Money: budgets, pricing, costs, revenue, payments, forecasts, financial reporting.
Legal exposure: contracts, compliance, licensing, liability, regulation, privacy law.
Building software: architecture, code, APIs, infrastructure, deployment, defects.
How something looks or is used: visual design, user experience, wireframes, brand assets, typography.
Reaching an audience: campaigns, channels, positioning, messaging, growth, brand.
Winning customers: pipeline, proposals, negotiations, customer calls, quotas, renewals.
What to build and why: roadmaps, feature decisions, user research, prioritisation, release scope.
Running the business day to day: process, vendors, logistics, internal tooling, procurement.
The people in the organisation: hiring, onboarding, performance, roles, staff policies.
Where the organisation is going: plans, market analysis, competitive positioning, long-range goals.
Protecting systems and data: access control, vulnerabilities, incidents, audits, threat models.
Gathering evidence before deciding: market research, interviews, literature reviews, experiments.
Helping existing customers: tickets, complaints, help-desk answers, escalations, satisfaction, troubleshooting.
Measuring and analysing: metrics, dashboards, SQL, experiments, tracking, statistics, reporting on numbers.
Working with other organisations: partners, integrations, resellers, agencies, joint ventures, sponsorship.
Raising and reporting to funders: fundraising, cap tables, investor updates, grants, valuation.
Meeting rules: audits, certifications, GDPR, policies, regulatory filings, risk registers.
Models and agents: LLMs, prompts, training data, evaluation, AI agents, automation with AI.
Making things to publish: articles, blog posts, video, copywriting, editorial calendars, social media.
People around the product: users, forums, Discord, ambassadors, feedback, events for members.
Explaining how things work: guides, manuals, READMEs, runbooks, API references, onboarding docs.
Gatherings: conferences, meetups, webinars, workshops, trade shows, travel and logistics.
Teaching and learning: courses, tutorials, curricula, coaching, certification, learning material.
Distributed ledgers: Cardano, wallets, tokens, smart contracts, NFTs, staking, on-chain payments.
Find, reproduce, or fix a defect where existing behavior differs from the expected result.
Respond to a service disruption, assess its impact, restore service, or document the incident.
Test a hypothesis with a trial or comparison and use the result to decide what to try next.
Choose between alternatives and record the trade-offs behind the choice.
Transfer ownership of work with the context and next steps the recipient needs.

SELECT "shared"."subscription"."id", "shared"."subscription"."createdAt", "shared"."subscription"."updatedAt", "shared"."subscription"."plan", "shared"."subscription"."referenceId", "shared"."subscription"."stripeCustomerId", "shared"."subscription"."stripeSubscriptionId", "shared"."subscription"."status", "shared"."subscription"."periodStart", "shared"."subscription"."periodEnd", "shared"."subscription"."trialStart", "shared"."subscription"."trialEnd", "shared"."subscription"."cancelAtPeriodEnd", "shared"."subscription"."cancelAt", "shared"."subscription"."canceledAt", "shared"."subscription"."endedAt", "shared"."subscription"."seats", "shared"."subscription"."billingInterval", "shared"."subscription"."stripeScheduleId" FROM "shared"."subscription" WHERE ("shared"."subscription"."periodEnd" = $1 AND "shared"."subscription"."periodStart" = $2 AND "shared"."subscription"."plan" = $3 AND "shared"."subscription"."referenceId" = $4 AND "shared"."subscription"."stripeSubscriptionId" IS NULL) ORDER BY "shared"."subscription"."updatedAt" DESC LIMIT $5 OFFSET $6
